description.value: The Orpheum is a grand 1927 concert hall in downtown Vancouver, best known as the permanent home of the Vancouver Symphony Orchestra, the largest performing arts organization in Western Canada. Designed by architect B. Marcus Priteca, the 2,672-seat auditorium retains its original opulence — sweeping staircases, Romanesque and Gothic arches, a domed ceiling mural, and a giant crystal chandelier. Originally a vaudeville house, it has hosted performers ranging from Fred Astaire to world-touring classical ensembles and is a National Historic Site.

enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: The Orpheum is one of Vancouver's most iconic cultural landmarks and a legitimate destination attraction for touring cyclists; it has confirmed washrooms and nearby Mobi bike-share infrastructure, making it a useful directory entry for cyclists planning visits.
enrichment_extras.notes: The website mentions Mobi bike-share stations 'at and nearby' the venue (www.mobibikes.ca). A hearing assist RF system is available free at coat check with ID/credit card deposit. Elevator access is via the Smithe Street entrance only.
